passages.1: The data center buildout is now 2% of GDP, reaching the size of the railroads, cars, highways, and telecoms.
passages.2: We build more data centers than offices.
passages.4: Nvidia is at the center of the data center buildout. Chip production has 10x’ed from 2M H100e to over 20M H100e.
passages.5: This has increased their revenue from $100B to $300B a year.
passages.6: Nvidia is making over 50% of all company’s revenues from GenAI.
passages.7: Plus, they’re doing so with never-before-seen operating margins. They have 66% operating margins compared to 33% for GAFA.
passages.8: And an annualized profit of $250B compared to $125B for GAFA.
passages.9: This is even more impressive when you compare it to previous eras. IBM, Wintel, and GAFA had around 25% margin. Nvidia has averaged 56%.
passages.10: Nvidia is a really good business. Which is why its market cap has 15x’ed from $300B to $5T, and they’ve become the most valuable company in the world.
passages.11: Now everyone else wants part of the GPU pie. Nvidia’s margin is the rest of the industry’s opportunity.
passages.13: …So what’s the actual opportunity here? Has Nvidia already eaten all the profits? Likely not.
passages.14: From 2020 to 2025, we built 10 GW+ of data center capacity. Nvidia GPUs filled 70% of them.
passages.15: But we’re likely to 10x to 100 GW by 2040.
passages.16: It’s easy to add a bar to a chart.
passages.17: It’s hard to actually build a gigawatt.
passages.19: It has giga in the name.
passages.20: It’s 1,000,000 US homes. The electricity for a whole city.
passages.21: It’s tough to know how many data centers will actually get built and wired up.
passages.23: But their data center permit database only shows 32 GW by 2028.
passages.24: Here are the biggest datacenters this decade.
passages.25: Part of this is a permitting issue. By 2028, a16z net new estimates are: 44 GW planned, 25 GW permitted, 19 GW shortfall.
passages.26: Part of this is an electricity issue: the US is at 0.52 TW of average electricity output, trying but failing (but trying!) to get to 2 TW. While China is at 1.21 TW, planning to get to 8 TW by 2040.
passages.27: In any scenario, expect 100 GW of data centers soon, mostly in the US and China.
passages.28: All of these data centers will need GPUs.
passages.29: Thus far, Nvidia has kept its market share as the main provider—around 70% of a growing pie.
passages.30: But going forward, this pie is up for grabs.
passages.31: Each GW powers ~$40B of chips. As we get more efficient, each GW will power ~$4B.
passages.32: So roughly the opportunity here is: 100 GW * $20B/GW = $2T opportunity to build chips.
passages.33: Many companies are trying to soak up Nvidia’s margin here.
passages.34: 1. Hyperscalers like Amazon Trainium and Google TPUs.
passages.35:
The Trainium 3 might become the Amazon Basics of GPUs. Anthropic committed to 5 GW of compute through AWS. Lots will be Nvidia chips (see new 2M GPU Amazon-Nvidia commitment), but lots will be Trainium chips.

Google might be getting out of the foundation model game to focus entirely on GCP (Gemini is Cooked but GCP is Cooking). They’re expanding their TPU lineup into training (8t) vs. inference (8i).

Roughly speaking, I see Trainium and TPUs as fighting for the training, not inference, market.
passages.36: 2. Startups like Cerebras (~$44B market cap), Etched ($21B valuation), and Samba Nova ($11B valuation).
passages.37:
Most of these (decacorn-sized) startups are focused on inference.

Cerebras is going to add 750MW of ultra-low latency chips to power ChatGPT’s new Ultrafast mode. On Ultrafast, Sol 5.6 answered 2,500 HLE questions in 11 hours vs. Claude Fable 5 in 78 hours. In other words, “Ultrafast worked through the frontier of human knowledge in a single working day.” (!!!)

Etched is building frontier inference clusters that break up then optimize pre-fill and decode. Pre-fill is compute-constrained, so they’re compute maxxing by voltage minimizing (LVI). Decode is memory-constrained, so they’re building Cluster Scale Memory with a better NVLink, so larger clusters can decode at once. As their founders said recently on Invest Like The Best, it’s crazy that training clusters like Colossus are 100,000 chips networked together, while inference clusters are still just eight chips.
passages.39:
OAI released Jalapeño’s first results at the end of August. It’s also focused on inference.

And damn, it’s impressive. It’s Pareto-dominant against GB200s and VR200s at tokens/s and tok/s/MW:

OpenAI bought 40% of all DRAM. Then used their own models for chip design. There are a few great articles analyzing their design (1, 2). Fundamentally, I understand it as a chip that is not optimized for training, nor even optimized for inference generally. It’s a decode-first, watt-minimizing chip, optimized for efficiently streaming 1 TB of model weights out of HBM.

provenance.1: Approximate coordinate readings from Redpoint chart. AI curves are scenarios. Axis calibrated piecewise to the source’s early and modern date spacing, then redrawn on a linear year axis.
provenance.2: Approximate color-traced lines from Joseph Politano image. Observed image ends mid-2025. User-requested dashed extrapolation through Aug 2026 uses a least-squares slope over each series’ final 12 months, anchored at its final observed point. Extrapolation is not reported data.
provenance.4: Epoch AI CSV, updated Aug 27 2026. Cumulative H100-equivalent compute medians, all records up to each quarter; incomplete data retained and marked in final quarter.
provenance.5-6: Approximate pixel measurements from Exponential View source. Units converted from $million to $billion. Subpixel bars are null, not zeros. Revenues are not deduplicated.
provenance.7-8: Exact values from original editable Nvidia profitability chart. IBM uses pretax proxy. OpenAI private-company figures; Anthropic positive adjusted operating income, amount not disclosed. GAFA means in prose are not totals.

9.profitBasis: GAAP net income, adjusted to 2026 dollars with CPI-U
9.aggregation: Wintel = Microsoft + Intel; GAFA = Alphabet/Google + Apple + Meta + Amazon
9.marginNote: Rounded period-weighted operating-margin estimates copied from the original chart; not derived from the net-income series.
9.provenance: Original chart from Find current Nvidia margins, August 28, 2026. Prototype reuses its data without a fresh financial audit.

provenance.29-30: Epoch AI chip-sales CSV: cumulative total chip TDP shares through Q1 2026. Future allocation is intentionally unspecified.
provenance.31-32: Author estimates: $40B/GW today, $4B/GW efficiency endpoint; separate midpoint scenario $20B/GW × 100 GW = $2T. Squares represent 1 GW each.

marketcap.note: Source historical chart samples, January 1999–August 2026. First sample January 29, 1999, following the January 22 IPO. Straight segments connect observations. Source m values multiplied by 100,000, as in its chart renderer.

opportunity.notes: Rounded figures and scenarios supplied in the article. Zero in 2020 is a baseline for additions since 2020, not zero installed global capacity. The 100 GW bars are scenarios, not reported construction. The 32 GW figure represents the subset in the cited permit database.

centers.notes: Top 10 centers by IT power at each point in Epoch AI timelines, 2023–2030. Linear interpolation between dated milestones; future values are project estimates, not completed capacity. Sites absent before their first milestone are not ranked. Each site holds its last recorded value thereafter.

permits.notes: a16z net-new figures as quoted by the author. Shortfall = 44 minus 25 GW.

electricity.notes: Historical annual total electricity generation from OWID, Ember and Energy Institute, 1999–2025. TWh divided by annual hours (8,760; 8,784 in leap years) gives average TW output, not installed nameplate capacity. Future dashed extensions are author estimates of 2 TW US and 8 TW China by 2040, linearly joined to the latest observations.

investmentAIScenarios.method: Pointwise median (midpoint of the two source scenarios), linearly interpolated at their combined year anchors. Shared pre-divergence history retained.
